content.comment_body: Hello, Please excuse me as I am using an online translator. I purchased a [company_name] [product_name] and have a question. I want users to be able to operate the front buttons of the [product_name]. Specifically, they should be able to choose a preset timer and press OK to start the program. Is this achievable? Thank you for your help. Regards, [user_name]. Edit: I speak French if needed.
Hello [user_name], you can edit parameters and adjust the timer settings. You can also use a software button to activate the timer.

Hello, thank you for your reply. If I understood correctly, it seems I can't use the physical face buttons, like the arrow keys or OK button, and only software buttons are available? Apologies, the translation via Google is tricky. To clarify, this is a medical device where the user needs to pick a duration from preset options, using two buttons to select and a third to start the program. I appreciate your help :-)

Hi [user_name], With [product_name] software you can set up messages with parameters, including a timer block. See the attachment for an example. You can change parameters by holding the ESC button for three seconds; a cursor will appear on the [product_name] display. You use the arrow keys to select which parameter to change, then press OK to enter edit mode and adjust values with the arrows.
Hello, thanks for your message! I will try this next week as all equipment is currently in use. I'll update you once I've tested it. Have a great weekend! Ciao ciao, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users asked how to control a [product_name] using front panel buttons to select predefined timer settings and trigger a program. Early replies brought some confusion on whether physical or software buttons could be used, but it was later clarified how parameters can be changed and functions activated using the hardware interface. The discussion points out inconsistencies and a lack of clarity in provided documentation about direct hardware interaction.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to operate the device with the front panel buttons (arrows, OK) for selecting preset times and starting the program, aiming for simple, hardware-based controls suitable for users without specialized training.
